newsitem.title: FIJI: Fiji hit by indefinite sugar strike.
newsitem.headline: Fiji hit by indefinite sugar strike.

text.p: Fiji's sugar workers on Monday began an indefinite strike over a 3.5 percent pay claim, closing the country's four sugar mills, local radio reported.

The Fiji Sugar Corporation has said it would not grant the pay rise, citing recent cyclone damage to crops and the uncertainty over the future of LOME, a European agricultural subsidy programme for developing countries.
The four mills -- Rarawai, Lautoka, Labasa and Penang -- were into the second month of crushing.
Fiji produced 4.3 million tonnes of sugarcane and 475,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1996.
Cyclone Gavin hit the country's canefields in March.
Fiji's sugar crush normally starts in June and runs through to December.
Fiji is a relatively minor sugar producer. Its 475,000 tonnes production in 1996 compared with 5.5 million tonnes production in Australia in 1996/97.
